subject: Pricing & marketplace path — mapping unit price across AWS/GCP/Azure
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@cloudry.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@cloudry.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: pricing & marketplace path from today’s call

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the call this morning — really helpful to see Redwood’s latency/cost controls and the routing options for private deployments. Procurement asked me to capture a few concrete items so we can start mapping to our vendor purchase path (we typically buy via marketplace private offers).

Quick recap of what we shared on our side (attached csv):
- Baseline: ~250M tokens/mo (conversational LLMs, avg 300 tokens/session)
- Peak months: up to ~420M tokens/mo (seasonal surge)
- Expected steady-state QPS: ~12 rps, spikes to ~40 rps for short periods
- Current internal target for unit economics: $80–$100 per 1M tokens (this is what product finance will greenlight)
- Procurement preference: AWS private offer first, open to GCP private pricing if parity can be shown; Azure is low priority

Two asks for Redwood to help procurement:
1) Map our token profile to a recommended unit price range for a 12–18 month reserved commit (show both hosted API and marketplace private-offer mapping).
2) Call out any Marketplace-specific limitations (e.g., per-SKU billing granularity, minimum term, billing lag, support contract implications).

Can you send a short matrix we can share with Procurement that shows immediate next-step pricing bands and an example private-offer line item (SKU/units) for AWS and GCP? Also include a list of documents Procurement will ask for (SOC2 evidence, billing contact, vendor codes).

Thanks — Alicia

--
Alicia Gomez
Head of Platform & Partnerships | Cloudry
A: +1 (415) 555-0192
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@cloudry.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 16:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: pricing & marketplace path from today’s call

Thanks Alicia — appreciate the clear ask and the volume profile (attached). Looping in Marissa (sales ops / marketplace mapping) and Sergio (partner integrations) so we can produce the matrix you can hand to Procurement.

Initial thoughts (high level):
- For the volume bands you shared, we can show two pathways: 1) Redwood Hosted API with committed monthly minimum (simple per-token billing + volume discount) and 2) Marketplace Private Offer mapping where we translate the committed tokens to SKU units for AWS/GCP and set a per-1M-token unit price.
- Based on similar deals, a realistic starting band to discuss with Procurement is $75–$110 per 1M tokens for a 12–18 month term depending on model family and cache/batching profile. The final unit price will change based on a) whether Cloudry wants currency-level committed spend (USD commit) vs token commit, and b) whether you need a legal SOW/managed support add-on.

Action items we’ll produce:
- A concise price matrix (AWS / GCP / Azure rows) mapping tokens->SKU->unit price and the assumptions behind CPU/GPU cost multipliers (attached: redwood_marketplace_matrix_v1.xlsx).
- Marketplace checklist for Procurement (SOC2, data residency, billing contact, sample private-offer agreement).
- A short example private-offer line item for AWS and GCP for a 12-month 300M tokens/mo commit and an escalated example for 420M tokens/mo.

Quick clarifying question for your procurement team: do they prefer quoting prices as $/1M tokens or as $/month committed (we can show both, but procurement often insists on per-month committed spend on private offers).

I’ll follow-up with the matrix tomorrow morning PST. If you want us to preview it with Procurement over a short call, we can set time next week.

Best,
Vivek
VP, Partnerships & GTM | Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@cloudry.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@cloudry.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 08:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: pricing & marketplace path from today’s call

Hi Alicia / Team — Marissa here on Sales Ops / marketplace mapping. Vivek thanks for the context — attaching a draft matrix (redwood_marketplace_matrix_v1.xlsx) and a short checklist. A few notes to make sure we map cleanly to AWS/GCP private-offer skus: 

Marketplace notes (short):
- AWS Private Offer: we typically create a custom SKU that represents 1M-token units or a monthly committed SKU (customer choice). AWS billing will ingest the SKU and produce monthly invoices tied to the Offer ID. Minimum term/commit is in the offer language — we typically do 12 or 36-months.
- GCP Marketplace: private pricing can be configured via a subscription/commit; GCP prefers dollar-based commits tied to a SKU unit. Mapping tokens -> dollars is expected and we provide suggested monthly commit values.
- Azure Marketplace: supports private pricing but has different onboarding timing; Azure often requires additional publisher enrollment.

Questions for Procurement (please reply inline):
1) For private-offer handling, do you want token-based SKUs (1M-token units) or dollar-based monthly SKUs?
2) What is your target contract term (12 / 18 / 36 months)?
3) Are there procurement constraints on invoicing cadence (monthly vs quarterly)?

If you can confirm those 3 items we’ll update the matrix with two explicit example Offers: one for AWS (1M-token SKU + unit price), one for GCP (monthly $ commit mapped to token equivalent).

Thanks — I’ll be standing by to update and send a clean PDF for Procurement.

--
Marissa Cole
Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@cloudry.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@cloudry.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: pricing & marketplace path from today’s call

Marissa — thanks, this is exactly what Procurement was asking for. Quick answers inline: 

1) Token vs dollar SKUs: Procurement prefers dollar-based monthly SKUs for internal budgeting, but they will accept token-based SKUs if you also provide a deterministic token->dollar mapping per month.
2) Contract term: leaning 12–18 months to start (procurement will approve 12 months faster).
3) Invoicing cadence: monthly invoicing is preferred.

Budget guardrails: finance has asked to target $85 per 1M tokens as our internal anchor; they’ll consider up to $100/1M if the offer includes strong latency SLOs, dedicated capacity guarantees, and a rollback/fallback model.

Procurement timeline: ~6–8 weeks for internal approvals + private-offer negotiation.

If you can produce two artifacts we’ll share internally: 1) a clean one-page matrix (AWS / GCP rows) that shows example Offer lines for 300M tokens/mo and 420M tokens/mo, priced both as $/1M tokens and as a monthly committed $ amount; 2) a short procurement checklist (SOC2 link, billing contact, sample offer).

Happy to hop on a quick 20-min sync with Procurement if that speeds review.

Best,
Alicia
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@cloudry.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@cloudry.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: pricing & marketplace path from today’s call

Great — thanks for the clarifications Alicia. Next steps from Redwood: 

1) We’ll send a one-page price matrix (AWS / GCP / Azure) with two example Offer lines:
   - Example A (conservative): 300M tokens/mo commit -> $95 / 1M tokens => ~$28,500 / month
   - Example B (stressed): 420M tokens/mo commit -> $88 / 1M tokens => ~$36,960 / month (volume discount reflected)
   Note: we’ll also show the equivalent dollar-based monthly SKU values (so Procurement can key them into their marketplace PO).

2) We’ll include the procurement checklist (SOC2 link, billing contact, legal contact, standard private-offer template) and highlight any marketplace-specific lead times per cloud.

3) Marissa will follow up with a PDF and upload the Drive link. If Cloudry wants a short 20-min sync with Procurement next Tue/Wed, we’re available — suggest Tue 10:00am PT.

Attaching updated matrix (redwood_marketplace_matrix_v1_updated.xlsx) and the checklist link: https://drive.redwood.com/marketplace/CLDY-price-matrix.

If anything above needs to change (different target $/1M, different term length) flag it here and we’ll regenerate numbers.

Best regards,
Vivek
